title: An agent shops on a merchant website with a Visa card: TAP browsing and payer signatures, a VIC token, verification at the CDN
summary: An agent enrolled in Visa Intelligent Commerce browses a merchant site with TAP agent-browser-auth signatures, has the consumer authenticate a purchase instruction with a passkey, creates it in VIC with an agent-specific token, then checks out with an agent-payer-auth signature and the agenticConsumer and agenticPaymentContainer body objects. A CDN verifies the header signatures at the edge; the merchant verifies the body objects and authorizes the card payment through its acquirer. The VIC API calls are named as Visa's visa/ai client names them.
specVersion: TAP spec, unversioned (read 2026-10-11, rechecked 2026-10-19); VIC API client in visa/ai (2026-09-30)

steps.label: Ask the agent to buy an item
steps.detail: The consumer asks the agent to find and buy one item on a merchant website. The consumer has already linked a Visa card to the agent.
steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: the agent platform records which merchants and amounts the consumer named.

steps.label: POST /vacp/v1/cards (card enrollment)
steps.detail: Visa Intelligent Commerce provisions an agent-specific payment token through the Visa Token Service, then runs issuer step-up where required and Visa Payment Passkey setup with device binding. The path is the one Visa's VIC API client in visa/ai calls; the request body is not shown because it is not public.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example. Path and host from Visa's VIC API client (visa/ai, 2026-09-30); body omitted.
POST /vacp/v1/cards HTTP/1.1
Host: sandbox.api.visa.com

steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: step-up verification of the cardholder and passkey setup in VIC.
steps.observable: Private: a bilateral call between the agent and Visa.

failures.condition: Step-up verification or passkey setup fails
failures.outcome: The card is not enabled for the agent, and no purchase instruction can be created.

steps.label: GET product page, signed with tag agent-browser-auth
steps.detail: The agent signs its browsing request with RFC 9421. Signature-Input covers at least @authority and @path and carries created, expires, keyid, alg, nonce and tag. Each request gets a fresh nonce; within one request, the header signatures and any signed body objects share it. The values here are placeholders, not the specification's examples, which cannot verify.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, TAP spec (unversioned). Placeholder values; not a test vector.
GET /product/trail-runner HTTP/1.1
Host: shop.example
Signature-Input: sig2=("@authority" "@path");created=1791763200;keyid="agent-key-1";alg="Ed25519";expires=1791763500;nonce="bm9uY2UtcGxhY2Vob2xkZXI";tag="agent-browser-auth"
Signature: sig2=:c2lnbmF0dXJlLXBsYWNlaG9sZGVy:

specRef.section: Agent Recognition Signature; Sample Browsing Request

steps.controlPoint: At signing: the agent platform can cover @method and a Content-Digest beyond the minimum, and refuse to sign for merchants the consumer did not pick.
steps.observable: Private: Signature-Input and Signature are visible only to the CDN, the merchant and intermediaries on the path.

failures.condition: A checkout enabler or proxy strips the signature headers
failures.outcome: The request arrives untagged and is treated as an unknown bot.

steps.label: Fetch the key for keyid
steps.detail: The CDN looks up the public key by keyid in its cache or fetches it from Visa's key store at a well-known URL. The specification named https://mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks until October 2026 and names no URL today. On 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19 that JWKS held one 2048-bit RSA key with a certificate for vic-oauth-jwe.visa.com from a Visa sandbox issuing CA, and no Ed25519 key, so the specification's example keyid cannot be resolved there; Visa's own code uses that key to encrypt tokens for its MCP server. How production agent keys are distributed is not published.

payload.content:
# Request to the JWKS the TAP specification named until October 2026 (it now names none).
GET /.well-known/jwks HTTP/1.1
Host: mcp.visa.com

steps.observable: Public: anyone can poll that JWK Set (cache-control public, max-age=3600) and watch keys appear or disappear.

failures.condition: No key for keyid, or the key has expired
failures.outcome: Block the request; TAP has no revocation list or key status endpoint.

steps.label: Verify tag, fields, window, nonce and signature
steps.detail: In the order the specification gives: a TAP tag is present, all minimum fields are present, created is past, expires is future and the two are at most 8 minutes apart, the nonce is new if the verifier keeps a record, the key is found, and the signature verifies over the rebuilt signature base.
steps.controlPoint: At the edge: keep a shared nonce record for at least 8 minutes, reject longer windows, check that the tag fits the page type.
steps.observable: Private to the zone owner. Cloudflare exposes cf.bot_management.signed_agent for Web Bot Auth agents (Enterprise Bot Management); whether TAP results appear there is not documented.

failures.condition: Neither agent-browser-auth nor agent-payer-auth in Signature-Input
failures.outcome: Not signed by a trusted agent; block or apply ordinary bot policy.

failures.condition: Missing field, window over 8 minutes, reused nonce or failed signature

steps.label: Forward as a verified browsing agent
steps.detail: The CDN forwards the request marked as a trusted agent that is browsing. The merchant may still limit what the agent can do.

steps.label: 200 product page with final cost
steps.detail: The merchant answers with product details, availability and the final cost after taxes and shipping, possibly as a simpler agent-specific page.

steps.label: Authenticate the purchase instruction with a passkey
steps.detail: The agent asks the consumer to authenticate the purchase instruction with a Visa Payment Passkey or another issuer-approved method. The verification result travels to VIC inside the next request; without it the agent cannot retrieve payment credentials.
steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: user consent and step-up, held by VIC.

failures.condition: The consumer declines or the passkey check fails
failures.outcome: No instruction is created and no credentials can be retrieved; nothing is charged.

steps.label: POST /vacp/v1/instructions (Payment Instruction with the authentication result)
steps.detail: The agent creates the Payment Instruction in VIC for this purchase. Visa's client sends the consumer's verification result (assuranceData) inside this request. Spending limits and consent live here, not in TAP.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example. Path and host from Visa's VIC API client (visa/ai, 2026-09-30); body omitted.
POST /vacp/v1/instructions HTTP/1.1
Host: sandbox.api.visa.com

steps.controlPoint: Before authorization: the instruction is where amount and merchant limits can be set.
steps.observable: Private: bilateral between the agent and Visa.

steps.label: POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/credentials
steps.detail: The agent retrieves the payment credentials for the approved instruction: the agent-specific token data it will present at checkout.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example. Path and host from Visa's VIC API client (visa/ai, 2026-09-30); body omitted.
POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/credentials HTTP/1.1
Host: sandbox.api.visa.com

steps.observable: Private: credentials pass only between Visa and the agent.

steps.label: POST checkout, signed with tag agent-payer-auth, with agenticConsumer and agenticPaymentContainer
steps.detail: The agent key-enters the card data in the merchant's guest checkout and signs the request with the payer tag. The body carries agenticConsumer (nonce, idToken, contextualData, kid, alg, signature) and agenticPaymentContainer (nonce, kid, alg, signature, plus a payment credential hash for key-entered guest checkout). Both objects are signed with the same key as the header and repeat this request's fresh nonce. The minimum header signature does not cover the body.

specRef.section: Sample Checkout Request; Consumer Recognition; Payment

steps.controlPoint: At signing: send consumer data only to the merchant the consumer chose; cover @method and Content-Digest where the merchant accepts them.
steps.observable: Private: body objects carry personal and card data for the merchant only.

failures.condition: The body is altered in transit
failures.outcome: The header signature still verifies; only the body object signatures can catch it.

steps.label: Verify the payer signature at the edge, forward
steps.detail: The CDN repeats the header checks for the agent-payer-auth tag and forwards the request. A CDN that protects only product paths would let an unsigned checkout through, as the sample proxy does.
steps.controlPoint: At the edge: verify every path that matters, including checkout and API routes.

failures.condition: The agent signed the checkout before the passkey approval and the 8-minute window ran out
failures.outcome: Block; the agent signs a fresh request with a new nonce.

steps.label: Verify the body objects and the credential hash
steps.detail: For each object the merchant checks required fields, compares its nonce with the header nonce, locates the key for kid and verifies the signature over the other fields in the order received. It hashes the key-entered card data and compares the result with the payment credential hash. It may map the obfuscated email or phone in the ID Token to an account it holds.

specRef.section: Consumer Recognition; Payment; Processing of Payment Data

steps.controlPoint: At the edge (merchant side): do not use consumer or payment data that fails verification, although TAP leaves the consumer object to merchant discretion.

failures.condition: Payment container fields missing, nonce mismatch or bad signature
failures.outcome: Should not be used for payment.

failures.condition: The merchant's hash of the key-entered card data differs from the payment credential hash
failures.outcome: The specification says the merchant should decline.

steps.label: Authorize the card payment
steps.detail: The merchant authorizes the agent-specific token through its acquirer as an ordinary card-not-present payment. TAP specifies nothing in this step; issuer and network risk decisions apply.
steps.controlPoint: At settlement: issuer and network risk decisions on the agent-specific token; Visa says TAP telemetry feeds its fraud and risk models.

failures.outcome: An ordinary card decline; TAP has no role.

steps.label: Order confirmation
steps.detail: The merchant returns the checkout result. TAP defines no receipt object.

steps.label: POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/confirmations
steps.detail: The agent reports the transaction outcome to Visa. Visa's VIC page said (archived 2026-10-03) that the commerce signals VIC collects allow quick resolution of most disputes; its workflows page says Visa retains this confirmation data for disputes.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example. Path and host from Visa's VIC API client (visa/ai, 2026-09-30); body omitted.
POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/confirmations HTTP/1.1
Host: sandbox.api.visa.com

steps.controlPoint: After the fact: VIC confirmations, the merchant's own logs of verification results, and ordinary card dispute rules.
steps.observable: Private: bilateral between the agent and Visa.
